Sonos iPhone app just got a major feature: Live Activities. Here's how it works.

Sonos app's Live Activities feature officially launches, letting users control playback from the lock screen

Sonos users have been through quite a few changes with the iOS app over the past few years.

After a controversial app redesign that ultimately led to the firing of the CEO, Sonos has been slowly adding back the features users have asked for.

Live Activities has been a feature users have long been hoping Sonos would add, and today it's finally rolling out in the latest update to the Sonos iOS app.

Here are the details, based on Sonos's post on Reddit:

How Live Activities works and what it looks like: Once enabled, as soon as you start playing audio and close the app, a Live Activity will appear and show the last room or group you played audio in. Once playback stops, the Live Activity will disappear after 15 minutes. While you can view the Live Activity on the iOS lock screen, you'll need to unlock your iPhone with Face ID or your passcode first before changing playback settings.

Bloomberg reported as early as February this year that Sonos was working on Live Activity support, so it's great to see the feature officially launch today.

If you don't want to use Live Activities, you can turn it off in the app's settings. Sonos also noted the following caveats:

  • Album artwork isn't currently included in the Live Activity, but the company says it is "exploring other ways to enhance the lock screen experience."
  • Live Activities will also work on CarPlay and Apple Watch, but with limited functionality. Sonos says "playback controls aren't supported at this time."
  • If you like to start playback outside of the Sonos app, such as through AirPlay, Bluetooth, or supported streaming services, playback controls are still available.

More details are available in the Reddit post here.

If you're looking to pick up more Sonos products, head over to Amazon. The Sonos Move 2 is currently $100 off.

What do you think about Sonos's support for Live Activities? Let us know in the comments.
